intro.name: A special council
intro.text:
After a string of disastrous experiments, (Subject) proposes forming a special council dedicated to investigating ideas that everyone else considers absurd. (Friend) points out that this describes nearly every idea (Subject) has ever had.
"Precisely!" says (Subject). "We are already experts."

question.name: The council
question.text: The council would accept proposals from any villager, including children, but would need clear rules about money, materials, and safety.

choices.label: Establish the council with strict testing rules.
Let the council operate freely for one day.
Reject the council but invite one proposal.

a1.name: A1
a1.text: The council's first proposal is a better way to tie bundles of firewood. Nobody is impressed until the farmers discover that the knot saves time. (Subject) unveils a grand banner reading THE DEPARTMENT OF TERRIBLE IDEAS. (Friend) asks whether the name is still appropriate. "More than ever," (Subject) says. "We have proved that terrible ideas deserve investigation."

a2.name: A2
a2.text: The council produces a thick list of regulations. Rule One: Do not test bridges with people standing on them. Rule Two: Do not taste unknown powders. Rule Three: Do not borrow the healers' supplies without asking. Rule Four: Do not add a goat to an experiment merely because a goat is available. (Subject) objects vehemently to Rule Four. The council adopts it unanimously.

a3.name: A3
a3.text: A child proposes a small shelter that keeps seedlings shaded during the hottest part of the day. The adults politely explain why it might fail. The child asks to test it anyway. A week later, the sheltered seedlings are thriving. (Subject) announces that the child is a genius. The child asks whether that means (child.he/she) can skip chores. It does not.

a4.name: A4
a4.text: (Subject) discovers that the council requires records, receipts, and meetings. (subject.He/she) spends the entire week writing proposals about how to reduce the amount of writing required for proposals. The first suggestion is to appoint a second secretary. The second secretary immediately resigns. (Friend) quietly enjoys the spectacle.

a5.name: A5
a5.text: Most proposals fail, but the villagers learn to ask better questions and to record what happened rather than what they hoped would happen. At the season's end, (Subject) presents a book containing twenty-nine failures and one useful discovery. "A poor record," (subject.he/she) admits. "A splendid beginning," replies (Friend).

b1.name: B1
b1.text: A goat wanders past the cooking fire. (Subject) ties a long wooden spoon to a loose frame beside it, hoping the goat's tail will stir a pot. The goat walks away. The spoon falls into the soup. The cook declares the experiment over and bans (Subject) from the kitchen until further notice.

b2.name: B2
b2.text: The back-scratching chair works perfectly. Unfortunately, its wooden fingers continue scratching after the sitter stands up. The chair scratches the air for several minutes before its vine cord unwinds. (Subject) calls it tireless. (Friend) calls it haunted. The chair is retired before anyone tries to improve it with sharper fingers.

b3.name: B3
b3.text: The villagers erect a frightening statue intended to scare away storms. That night, rain pours over the entire village. (Subject) announces that the statue has worked: "The storm was so frightened it wept!" (Friend) asks whether there is any result (Subject) would consider failure. (Subject) thinks carefully. "No," (subject.he/she) admits.

b4.name: B4
b4.text: (Subject) unveils a basket designed to roll downhill by itself. It does. Unfortunately, the basket rolls directly into a pond. (Subject) declares that this proves the principle of effortless transport. The fishermen return the basket and ask that the next demonstration take place farther from their nets.

b5.name: B5
b5.text: A proposal to grow square coconuts divides the village. The builders want fruit that stacks neatly. The farmers insist that trees do not care about storage. The cooks ask whether the fruit will taste different. (Subject) finally produces a wooden box and places an ordinary coconut inside. "BEHOLD!" (subject.he/she) cries. "A square coconut container!" The council votes to award (Subject) half a prize for solving half a problem.

b6.name: B6
b6.text: By sunset, the village has acquired a frog alphabet, three broken stools, a basket in a tree, and a handwritten petition demanding that (Subject) stop calling everything a breakthrough. (Subject) announces that the day has been an overwhelming success because nobody can remember being bored. (Friend) admits that this, at least, is true.

c1.name: C1
c1.text: The single proposal is a simple tool for lifting hot cooking pots without burning one's hands. The cook tests it and approves. (Subject) is so shocked that (subject.he/she) forgets to make a speech. (Friend) quietly writes down the date for future generations.

c2.name: C2
c2.text: (Subject) proposes putting a roof over the ocean to prevent rain from wetting the fish. (Friend) asks how much wood this would require. (Subject) answers, "All of it." The council rejects the proposal. (Subject) accuses them of lacking ambition. The builders accuse (Subject) of lacking an understanding of oceans.

c3.name: C3
c3.text: A shy villager suggests hanging small bells along a path to help people find their way in darkness. The council initially laughs, imagining an entire forest of bells. Then a healer points out that a few bells near an important turn might genuinely help. The idea is tested on a short, safe path. (Subject) is delighted that someone else's absurdity has become useful.

c4.name: C4
c4.text: The proposal is presented with great ceremony. An elder recognizes it immediately as a tool used by (elder.his/her) grandparents. (Subject) is crushed. "So I invented nothing?" (subject.he/she) asks. "You rediscovered something worth remembering," replies the elder. The villagers invite the elder to teach the forgotten method.

c5.name: C5
c5.text: The council rejects the proposal but asks (Subject) to return next season with a better-tested version. (Subject) agrees, then produces a second bundle of sketches from beneath (subject.his/her) cloak. (Friend) stares in horror. "I thought we were only considering one idea!" "We are," says (Subject). "These are merely its forty-seven improvements." The meeting ends immediately.
